## Load packages for this project

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(ggpubr)
library(broom)
```

## Import clinical data and visualize raw data

Raw data is imported and pivoted into a long data frame for data visualization and analysis.

Visualize degrees of off vertical center as a function of time of for patient, then map colour to "exercise" variable to show how exercising affects balance of each patients with or without drug.

The combined figure using plot_grid() at the end of this code chunk will answer first part of Question 1

```{r}
load("data/gait.Rda")

# Convert this table into a tidy "long" data frame:
clean_gait_data <- gait_data %>% pivot_longer(cols = 5:last_col(),
                           names_to = "Time_of_measurement_seconds",
                           values_to = "Degrees_off_vertical_orientation" )

# Then convert values in the column "Times of measurement" into numeric time.
clean_gait_data <- clean_gait_data %>% mutate(Time_of_measurement_seconds = sub("_.*", "", Time_of_measurement_seconds))

# convert time of measurement to numeric
clean_gait_data <- clean_gait_data %>% 
  mutate(Time_of_measurement_seconds = as.numeric(Time_of_measurement_seconds))

# Plot raw data for patients receiving L-DOPA control compound
plot_old_compound <- clean_gait_data %>% 
  filter(treatment == "L-DOPA control") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Time_of_measurement_seconds, Degrees_off_vertical_orientation, fill = exercise))+
  geom_col()+
  guides(fill = "none")+
  facet_wrap(~donorid)+
  labs(title = "L-DOPA",
       x = "Time of measurement (s)",
       y = "Degrees off vertical orientation")+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 350, 700),
                     labels = c("0", "350", "700")
                     )+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-60,60))+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 40, b = 20, l = 40),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 5)
        )



# Plot raw data for patients receiving new compound
plot_new_compound <- clean_gait_data %>% 
  filter(treatment == "New compound") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(Time_of_measurement_seconds, Degrees_off_vertical_orientation, fill = exercise))+
  geom_col()+
  labs(y = "")+
  facet_wrap(~donorid)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 350, 700),
                     labels = c("0", "350", "700")
                     )+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-60,60))+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "New compound",
       x = "Time of measurement (s)")+
  scale_fill_discrete(breaks = c("y","n"),
                        labels = c("Yes", "No"),
                        name = "Exercise")+
  theme(
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 40, b = 20, l = 40),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 5)
  )

# Combined two plots into the same figure. 
plot_grid(plot_old_compound, plot_new_compound)
          



  
```

## Calculate descriptive statistics for each patients

```{r}
summary_data <- clean_gait_data %>% 
group_by(donorid, treatment, exercise,age) %>% 
  # because the measure have negative values, all values are converted to positive before calculating the mean
  summarise(avg_imbalance = mean(sqrt(Degrees_off_vertical_orientation^2)),
            median_imbalance = median(sqrt(Degrees_off_vertical_orientation^2)),
            sd_imbalance = sd(Degrees_off_vertical_orientation)
            ) 
# This table contains summary data for each patient,
summary_data
```

## Plot each summary statistics of patients against treatment

In this section I plot the three summary statistics (mean, median and standard deviation) of each patient against treatment status to examine how different parameter capture the effect of treatment.

The three summary statistics parameters capture the effect of treatment equally, so the mean will be used for further data investigation.

```{r}

plot_stat <- function(object, title){
  summary_data %>% 
    ggplot(aes(treatment, object))+
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), linewidth = 1)+
    geom_point(size = 1)+
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Treatment",
         y = "")+
    ylim(0,18)+
    theme_classic(base_size = 16)+
    theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", face = "bold"),
          axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
          axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "inch"),
          plot.margin = margin(40, 20, 0,0),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 4)
    )
}

plot_grid(plot_stat(summary_data$avg_imbalance, "Mean of degrees off vertical axis"), plot_stat(summary_data$median_imbalance, "Median of degrees off vertical axis"), plot_stat(summary_data$sd_imbalance, "Standard deviation of degrees off vertical axis"))

  


```

Check if data is normally distributed within each group:

```{r}
#| warning: false
# First use QQ plot inspect distrubution of data
summary_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(sample = avg_imbalance))+
  geom_qq()+
  geom_qq_line()+
  facet_wrap(~treatment)

# Then use Shapiro-Wilk normality test to check if data is normally distributed in each treatment group:
summary_data %>% 
  filter(treatment =="L-DOPA control") %>% 
  pull(avg_imbalance) %>% 
  shapiro.test()

summary_data %>% 
  filter(treatment =="New compound") %>% 
  pull(avg_imbalance) %>% 
  shapiro.test()
```

Shapiro-Wilk test returns a p-value \>0.05 for both group and according to QQ plot, most data point sit on the line. So data is likely normally distributed. So t-test will be used to compared between two groups.

```{r}
summary_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(treatment, avg_imbalance))+
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), linewidth = 1)+
  geom_point(size = 1)+
  labs(
       x = "Treatment",
       y = "Mean of degrees off vertical orientation")+
  ylim(0,18)+
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)+
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", face = "bold"),
        axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
        axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "inch"),
        plot.margin = margin(40, 20, 0,30),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 4),
  )+
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = list(c("L-DOPA control", "New compound")),
    method = "t.test",
    label = "p.format"
  )


t.test(
  avg_imbalance ~ treatment,
  data = summary_data,
  var.equal = TRUE
)
```

T-test gives a p-value \<0.05, meaning there is statistical significant difference in gait between participants receiving L-DOPA and the new compound.

## Investigate how exercise affects drug effect

```{r}
summary_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(treatment, avg_imbalance, colour = exercise))+
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), linewidth = 1)+
  geom_jitter(position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.9)+
  theme_bw(base_size = 16)+
  scale_colour_discrete(name = "Exercise status",
                        breaks = c("y", "n"),
                        labels = c("Yes", "No"))+
  labs(x = "Treatment",
       y = "Imbalance (Mean of degrees off vertical centre)",
  )+
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", face = "bold"),
        axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
        axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "inch"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
        
  )

```

From the plot, apparently exercise status has a huge effect on balance. It seems to increase balance more than the drug itself and have a synergistic effect when combined with the drug.

To investigate how exercise status contribute alongside with drug treatment, a two-way ANOVA will be performed.

```{r}
# First, check normality of each group:

summary_data %>% 
  group_by(treatment, exercise) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(sample = avg_imbalance ))+
  geom_qq()+
  geom_qq_line()+
  facet_wrap(~treatment + exercise)
```

From the QQplot, it is relatively safe to assume that data in each group is normally distributed

Next run two-way ANOVA:

```{r}


anova_tbl <- aov(avg_imbalance ~ treatment * exercise,
    data = summary_data)

clean_ANOVA <- tidy(anova_tbl)

clean_ANOVA

write.csv(clean_ANOVA, file ="output/anova_table.csv")
```

The results of this test indicate, however, the effect on balance of exercise and treatment are likely independent of each other (p = 0.36). In other words, exercising itself does improve balance (p = 0.01), but likely not improve the effect of the drug.

Next we ask how age affects gait, using a linear regression model:

```{r}

# Build linear model for each treamtment group
fit_control <- lm(summary_data$avg_imbalance[treatment == "L-DOPA control"] ~ summary_data$age[treatment =="L-DOPA control"], data = summary_data)

fit_new_compound <- lm(summary_data$avg_imbalance[treatment == "New compound"] ~ summary_data$age[treatment =="New compound"], data = summary_data)

summary(fit_control)
summary(fit_new_compound)

# Extract residuals from linear model and check if they are normally distributed within each group
shapiro.test(resid(fit_control))
shapiro.test(resid(fit_new_compound))


# Scatter plot to visualize relalationship between Gait and age
  summary_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(age, avg_imbalance, colour = treatment))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_classic()+
  geom_smooth(method = lm)+
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", face = "bold"),
        axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.3),
        axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "inch")
  )+
    stat_regline_equation(
      aes(label = after_stat(eq.label)),
      label.x = 60,
      label.y = c(17, 16)    
    ) +
    stat_cor(
      aes(label = after_stat(p.label)),
      label.x = 66,
      label.y = c(17, 16)     
    )
```

Within each group, Shapiro's test on residiuals returns p value \>0.05, meaning residuals are normally distributed and hence linear regression model is valid.

In both treatment group, balance tends to get worse as age increases, (both groups have positive slope). However linear regression indicates this association is only statistically significant in the group treated with new compound (this group also has a higher slope). Overall, gait tends to decrease as the patient age, however this effects is likely independent from treatment.
